To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the framing of AI is atheoretic and anthropocentric, and therefore limited.
(a) MI is a better framing of intelligence than AI because it (i) is theoretical, (ii) is post-anthropocentrism, and (iii) is organicist emergentism, and (b) AI is a contributor to MI.
Framing of AI as a contributor to hybrid MI is a more effective approach than the current framing of AI as the cause of future events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
framing the future development of AI within the context of MI, which includes natural intelligence and AI as contributors.
the following questions: How might AI be re-framed to contribute to MI?
the following questions: What are the implications for AI development if AI is reframed within a MI framework?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MI is a more comprehensive framing of intelligence and its development, than is AI.
AI is a component of MI.
MI is the future of intelligence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AI can be seen as an emerging intelligence that is contributing to a multi-intelligence (hybrid) system.
MI can be defined as a system of intelligences, including human and other natural intelligences as well as artificial intelligences.
AI is one of many intelligences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AI should be considered as a contributor to a multi-intelligence hybrid being or system, not as a single-variable mechanism that is superior to all other forms of intelligence.
the future is not a single-variable mechanistic AI future but rather a multi-variable emergentist MI future.
AI is not an all-or-nothing phenomenon.
